summary.analyst:
Event: rundll32 was invoked with an obfuscated command consistent with confirmed malicious activity. Recovered payload reads: `rundll32.exe C:\Users\Public\evil.dll,StartW`, which corroborates that rundll32 was used as a launcher for downstream code rather than a routine administrative task.

Living-off-the-land use of rundll32 bypasses application-allowlisting because the binary itself is signed and trusted; the malicious intent lives in the arguments, not the executable. Investigation mapped the observed behaviour to T1218.011 · Rundll32, T1218 · System Binary Proxy Execution.

Supporting evidence, in weight order: LOLBAS · rundll32.exe [META-lolbas-001]; Rundll32 [N-004]; System Binary Proxy Execution [N-005]; LOLBIN · rundll32 [N-006]; LOLBIN detected: rundll32.exe [N-007]. Recovered network/host indicators cover 1 external domain(s).

Impact is confirmed malicious. Any endpoint that executed this payload should be considered compromised until proven otherwise. Scope of observed entities: 1 external domain(s).

No containment signal was observed in the submitted evidence (no quarantine, block, or prevent action was reported). This does not mean containment did not occur — it means the artefact submitted to NivXRay did not include that telemetry.

Recommended next actions: 1. Isolate affected hosts and block the identified indicators at the perimeter; 2. Preserve host artefacts and start forensic triage for the affected users.

## 1. Executive Summary

Verdict: **Malicious** (confidence 96%). No affected-host telemetry was included with this submission. Execution vector: rundll32. Network target: http(s)://lld.live.

*Sources — cio.verdict, cio.entities, cio.metadata.iocs, cio.evidence_graph*

## 2. Incident Overview

The submission triggered rundll32 with an obfuscated command that, once recovered, resolves to `rundll32.exe C:\Users\Public\evil.dll,StartW`. Aggregate evidence supports a **Malicious** verdict — the sample should be treated as attacker-controlled until proven otherwise.
